assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
caveats: Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 84.21%, order-level 87.07%, technical 86.56% (retries and drop-offs explain the gap).
The daily series for Kestrel Bank debit cards shown only runs to 18 September, so the pattern for 19-20 September is not visible.
The data-quality scan found no issues, but the cause of the timeouts is inferred from failure codes, not confirmed by acquirer logs.

facts.text: Card attempt success rate fell 2.54pp from 86.75% (28,534 attempts) to 84.21% (28,358 attempts). The change is statistically and practically significant.

By payment method, the mix effect is 0.00pp and the rate effect is -2.54pp. Debit card contributes -1.36pp, credit card -0.93pp and card EMI -0.25pp. Payment-method shares barely moved (debit 49.1% to 49.0%, credit 42.6% to 42.6%, EMI 8.4% to 8.4%).

Kestrel Bank is about 30% of card volume but accounts for -2.63pp (104%) of the -2.54pp change. Its success rate fell from 87.0% to 78.2%, a drop of 8.78pp. The other acquirers show no significant change: Meridian Bank +0.85pp, Northstar Bank -0.75pp and Saffron Bank 0.00pp.
Within Kestrel Bank, debit cards fell from 86.47% to 77.23% (-9.24pp, -1.36pp of the total) and credit cards from 88.74% to 80.56% (-1.04pp of the total).
Kestrel Bank debit card daily success rate was 86.96%, 87.55% and 85.45% on 14-16 September, then fell to 57.14% on 17 September and 55.52% on 18 September.
For Kestrel Bank debit cards, ACQ_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.22 to 10.21 per 100 attempts (9 to 433 failures). Other failure codes moved by less than 0.4 per 100 attempts.
Across all card attempts, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.22 to 3.04 per 100 attempts (63 to 863 failures), the largest increase of any failure code. The next largest was INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS at +0.23 per 100.
Every issuing bank shown fell by between 2.08pp and 2.93pp, so the decline is not specific to any issuer.

response.headline: Card success rate fell 2.54pp, from 86.75% to 84.21%, and the whole drop is a like-for-like rate decline, not a shift in payment-method mix; it is concentrated at one acquirer, Kestrel Bank, which fell 8.78pp.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Kestrel Bank for incident or maintenance logs from 17-18 September. Check ACQ_TIMEOUT counts by hour and by Kestrel route, and check whether the rate recovered after 18 September.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is almost entirely at Kestrel Bank (104% of the change), it begins abruptly on 17 September in the daily data, and ACQ_TIMEOUT, a technical acquirer code, jumped from 0.22 to 10.21 per 100 Kestrel debit attempts while other codes stayed flat.
hypotheses.text: A technical problem on the Kestrel Bank acquiring route (connectivity or processing) starting around 17 September caused authorisations to time out and drove most of the card success-rate drop.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Pull the failure-code shift for Kestrel Bank credit cards and confirm ACQ_TIMEOUT is the main increase.
hypotheses.rationale: Kestrel credit card success fell from 88.74% to 80.56%, a similar pattern to debit, but the failure-code breakdown was only provided for Kestrel debit cards.
hypotheses.text: Credit cards at Kestrel Bank were affected by the same timeout issue.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A technical problem on the Kestrel Bank acquiring route (connectivity or processing) starting around 17 September caused authorisations to time out and drove most of the card success-rate drop.
recommendations.rationale: Kestrel Bank accounts for essentially all of the 2.54pp drop, and its ACQ_TIMEOUT rate rose sharply.
recommendations.text: Escalate to Kestrel Bank to confirm the root cause of the ACQ_TIMEOUT spike on 17-18 September and obtain a fix or incident report.
